page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a 524 GB local SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests, consistently fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, the 64-vCPU allocation elevates multi-core performance to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Notably, memory bandwidth for large-block uncached read and write operations is strong, placing in the top 25%, which supports memory-intensive operations. Extended CPU instruction tests also perform in the top 25%, utilizing supported flags like AVX and AVX-512F. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64s_v3 offers a high-density resource profile suitable for enterprise workloads that require substantial parallel processing and memory capacity without needing the highest single-thread clock speeds. The combination of 256 GB RAM, a 524 GB local SSD, and Premium Storage capability makes this server well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database hosting, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or heavy large-model LLM text generation, where its performance falls into the lower tier.
